svg.title: How worker-policy routes work
svg.desc: Flowchart: an identity gate, partitioning into units, a bulk check, route_cost.py's hard-cap and margin checks, delegation, and a paid ladder picked by unit kind. The default ladder runs from local workers (disabled by default) to gpt-6-luna at high effort, gpt-6-luna at max, then gpt-6.1-sol at low; interpretation research joins it at gpt-6-luna max. Terminal units (debugging, testing, build, environment) and analysis research get gpt-6.1-sol at medium, then a fresh gpt-6.1-sol at medium whose brief carries the failure summary. When any ladder runs out, the orchestrator reviews the failure summaries and re-plans once or reports to the user. Break-glass is a separate exception path for broken delegation or safety and authority failures, never a ladder rung. After integration, code changes are measured with diff_stats.py and get at most one cleanup worker pass before the completion gate. Side panels explain the cost model and supervision rules.
svg.text: Sol and Astra plan, brief and integrate. Cheap Luna workers do the reading and writing.
